chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from his father, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who comes to a Mahram (close female relative) would be struck with a strike of the sword, taking from him what it takes (i.e., causing death or taking his life).'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.ذَاتَ مَحْرَمٍ: A close female relative with whom marriage is permanently forbidden

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a man who commits adultery with a close relative in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from Al-Kafi is often interpreted as indicating 'Rajm' (stoning) or a specific severe corporal punishment, with 'struck with a sword' serving as a metaphor for the decisive nature of the penalty for incest. The phrase 'took from him what it took' underscores the finality of the punishment, reflecting the high status of the Mahram relationship in Islamic law. This ruling highlights the unique gravity of incest compared to general adultery, a distinction emphasized by scholars like Al-Kulayni in his compilation.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbat, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from his father who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The one who comes to a Mahram would be struck with a strike of the sword, taking from him what it takes (lives or dies)’.
